content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 23. Supplemental: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 architecture description concepts. This unit focuses on traceability from concerns to architecture.

Traceability connects stakeholder concerns, scenarios, principles, decisions, views, implementation work, and verification evidence. It allows teams to answer why a design exists and whether it still satisfies the original need.
Traceability should be purposeful. Too much traceability becomes bureaucracy, but too little makes architecture impossible to evaluate or change safely.
Studio: trace one quality scenario through a decision, a view element, an implementation task, and a test or metric.

concepts.name: Architecture traceability
concepts.description: The ability to follow relationships from concerns and decisions to views, implementation, and evidence.

concepts.name: Trace link
concepts.description: An explicit connection between two architecture artifacts or between architecture and implementation evidence.

concepts.name: Verification evidence
concepts.description: A test, review, metric, prototype, or analysis result used to support an architectural claim.

concepts.name: Traceability burden
concepts.description: The maintenance cost created by recording and updating too many trace links.
